marks.gloss_en: תא שמע: רבי אילעאי אומר משום רבי ישמעאל: אנדרוגינוס בכור הוא ומומו עמו -- שמע מינה מיפשט פשיטא ליה!
ודילמא ״אם תימצא לומר״ קאמר! -- perhaps this too is said 'if you should say'
R' Ilai in R' Yishmael's name: an androginos is a firstborn, and its blemish is with it
תא שמע: זכר ולא נקבה ... להוציא טומטום ואנדרוגינוס; the baraita is R' Yishmael's, and a verse is needed to exclude only if the androginos is certainly male to him (41b.7)
the baraita: 'a male' -- and not a female; when it says 'a male' below, which is unneeded, why does it say it? to exclude a tumtum and an androginos
לעולם רבנן בתראי, וגבי בכור תרתי קראי כתיב: הזכר והזכרים
the stam: and of the firstborn two verses are written: 'the male' and 'the males'
ספיקא הוא, ואתי קרא למעוטי ספיקא? -- for him it is a doubt, and a verse does not come to exclude a doubt
the stam: does a verse come to exclude a doubt? (rhetorical: it does not -- used at 41b.5 and again at 41b.7)
מחד קרא נפקי, דהא גבי בכור חד זכר הוא דכתיב וקא ממעטי כולהו מינייהו -- they derive all three exclusions from one verse, whereas the baraita uses two
the baraita is the later Rabbis' (the Sages of the mishnah)
(horn 1) it is obvious to R' Yishmael that the androginos is a firstborn and its blemish is with it
the stam: what is the practical difference? to flog on its account for shearing and for work
rather, it is obviously R' Yishmael's
Rav Chisda: the dispute is over the androginos
אלא מעתה בערכין יערך? אלמה תניא: הזכר -- ולא טומטום ואנדרוגינוס! -- if the tumtum is [certainly male or female, only] in doubt, it should be valuated
